Preferred syntax: block. Fixed categorical cells; membership appears in comments.

Framing

This Pack groups the contracts used to iterate on a design through the graph, in review order. Its members cover concise recipe answers; rule keys, question fields and relation reasons; comparison between design passes; context bundles, perspectives and change proposals. The final members cover when implemented design detail may leave a Spec and how file-level imports inform anchor curation, drawing on lessons from the Protocol's predecessor, @libar-dev/architect.

Recipe answers fit an agent's context and explain their misses

spec:consumers.agent-surface.answer-shapesUse Case / Behavior · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 10 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

A usability trial gave agents only the skills, the recipe catalog and sdp q and a fixed set of delivery questions. Every answer was reachable without opening a carrier or source file. The agents repeatedly met oversized answers, unexplained misses, ambiguous next-rung labels and fields whose names overstated the relations they reported.

Intent
actor
An agent answering a delivery question through the catalog recipes.
problem
An agent spends calls trimming oversized answers, decoding terse misses and writing the same missing body, and can repeat a recipe's label as fact when the label says more than the graph does.
outcome
Let an agent get each answer in one call that fits its context, with every miss explained.
Behavior

5 unkeyed rules.

Design
detailParameter line 33 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md:33
recipes 4, 29, 35 and 54 read params.detail, absent or false for the summary and true for every row in full; recipe 29's and recipe 54's detail may also be a list of member ids, which returns full rows for those members and summary rows for the rest of the Pack, and an id that is not a member is a diagnostic in the result. A summary keeps totals as the full answer counts them and adds leftOut, one line for each kind of detail it omits.
impactSummary line 34 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md:34
{ changedFiles, totals, impactedSpecs: [id], impactedPacks: [id], atRisk: { incomingSpecs: [id], outgoingSpecs: [id], other: [id] }, coverageUnknownFiles, unlinkedUnits: [id], leftOut } is recipe 4's summary. Incoming and outgoing name the connecting edge's direction relative to the impacted node and assert no dependency, since the edge may be any type; a Spec reached both ways is listed in both, and other holds the at-risk nodes that are not Specs.

no citation recorded

impactDetail line 35 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md:35
With detail: true, recipe 4 returns full rows and reasons; every at-risk reason carries direction, incoming or outgoing, relative to its impacted end.

{ id, specKind, statedReadiness, floorReached, statedNextRung, holds: [{ clauseId, targets: [id] }], openQuestions, blockingQuestions, implementedBy, referencedBy } is recipe 29's summary row, with counts for the last four; the summary's boundary lists ids per direction, and totals is unchanged. holds is the summary of statedNextRungFailures, retaining each clauseId and target ids.

The Spec context carries statedNextRung when one exists and statedNextRungFailures; promotion preflight reads those fields and the floor's next rung without computing a floor, and renders a missing next rung as null.

catalogIndex line 41 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md:41

wrapIdiom line 42 · specs/consumers/agent-surface.answer-shapes.sdp.md:42
to filter a shipped answer, the caller wraps the shipped body in an async arrow function that takes params, inside its own body, const answer = await (async (params) => { <shipped body> })({ <the recipe's own parameters> });, and returns a filtered value, so the caller's own parameters never reach the recipe as names it does not take; the catalog shows the shell form and states that the caller's part must hold no shell expansion.

2. A rule or flow entry may carry a key that addresses it

spec:model.rule-keys

A rule or flow entry may carry a key that addresses it

spec:model.rule-keysBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design gave a behavior rule an optional id, so the rule could later be promoted to a Spec of its own, and an optional rationale (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §2.2). The Protocol kept promotion and dropped the id. An unkeyed rule has no address, so a review finding, a register row or an example cannot name it; a key gives it an address. Open questions carry optional keys on the entry-address key grammar; this Spec follows that pattern for rules.

Intent
problem
An inline rule has no identity but its position and its text, so anything outside the Spec that cites one rule breaks silently when the rules above it move or the rule is reworded.
outcome
Let an author key a rule or flow entry, so a review, a register row or an example can name the entry it is about.
Rule
rule line 27 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:27
Every entry of a Spec's primary behavior owner may carry an optional key on the open-question key grammar: the rule: and flow: entries of Behavior, the entries of Rule and Contract, and the entries and rule: entries of Workflow. One Spec keeps one key namespace across them, unique among its keyed entries, and an unkeyed entry stays lawful and has no address.
rule line 28 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:28
A key sits in a marker at the start of the entry's text, after the rule: or flow: label where the entry has one, as in - rule: [#graphOnly] The Studio is a projection. and - [#oneFamily] Every validator belongs to one family., the shape an open question's marker uses, so one form serves labelled and plain entries.
rule line 29 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:29
Every keyed entry is addressed as spec:<id>#rule.<key> whatever its section, because a Spec uses one primary behavior owner. The address resolves while the Spec carries an entry with that key and fails validation in every Spec that names it once the key is renamed or removed.
rule line 30 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:30
A rule address is refused in every id slot, as every entry address is, so no anchor targets a rule and no delivery fact attaches to one.
rule line 31 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:31
An example names the keyed rules it exercises on its verifies relation: the target is an object with target and exercises, a list of the verified Spec's rule keys, beside an optional reason. A key the verified Spec does not carry is a conformance error at the relation, as a missing entry address is. The list mints no edge and confers no delivery fact, so verifies stays whole-Spec, and a rule-coverage recipe reads it to report which keyed rules a bound example exercises and which none does.
rule line 32 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:32
A keyed entry carries its key and its text and nothing else; why a rule holds is the Spec's narrative, or a decision Spec named through decidedBy when the why passes the ADR three-part test.
rule line 33 · specs/model/rule-keys.sdp.md:33
A keyed rule promoted to a Spec of its own leaves its address behind, because promotion moves the content out, and every mention of that address fails until it names the new Spec.

Design view

Requirement drawing

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.checked-mentions

    A Spec id in narrative or section text, outside gwt and gwt-vocabulary fences, is a mention. A mention that does not resolve is a conformance error. A mention of another Spec that shares no declared relation with the mentioning Spec, in either direction, is one warning per mentioning Spec and target Spec pair, whatever the number of locations; an address on the mentioning Spec's own id is checked for its entry and never warned. An entry address is a Spec id followed by #, the section name design, ui, question, rule, or term, a dot, and the entry's lower-camel ASCII key, as in spec:<id>#design.<key> or spec:<id>#question.<key>. A design or ui address resolves when the Spec exists and that section holds the key as its own key, other than description; a question address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its open questions carries that key; a term address resolves when the Spec exists and one of its Model terms carries that key. The # sub-part is reserved for the entry address in every namespace: a Spec's own id, a relation target, a Pack member or model reference, an anchor id or target, and the specId and ref builders all refuse it. A mention mints no edge, and the reader gains no join.

  • spec:decisions.shipped-projections-frozen

    Re-specifying the shipped Design Review, census, Mermaid, or Gherkin projection is refused. These four projections are the ruled read surfaces over the one graph. A later decision Spec that supersedes this one replaces the ruling whole; a decision Spec that refines this one narrows it for one projection or one rendering and leaves the rest frozen. Either passes the ADR three-part test.

3. An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fields

An open question may name who decides it, its links, a provisional reading and a re-entry trigger

spec:model.open-question-fieldsBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · 2 decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design gave an open question an owner and a list of links to decision records, discussions and tickets, beside its text and its blocking flag (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §2.1). A question key gives a question an address and nothing more, so the first adopter keeps the rest beside the graph. Its decision register (libar-platform/design/decisions/register.json, described in design/advisors/register.md) records for each open decision its sources, who decides it as a class (tactical, delegated or owner) and an advisor lens, the provisional reading the design proceeds on, and a lean. It also records a status, the work unit it blocks, dates and who checked the lean. This Spec captures the part that states something about the question and leaves the work record outside.

A TypeScript open-question list that cannot be read statically drops whole, blocking questions included. A failure under one of the four fields is an error, because the fields arrived with no carrier relying on a lossy reading; a failure in a question's text, its blocking flag or the list itself keeps the warning every other non-static TypeScript section property gives.

Intent
problem
A question's text and blocking flag do not say who settles it, what it rests on, or what the design assumes until it is settled, so an adopter keeps a register beside the graph that repeats each question.
outcome
Let an open question carry who decides it, the sources it rests on, the reading the design proceeds on and, on a deferral, what brings it back, without a status.
risks
  • A field for who decides invites fields for when and for what state the question is in, which would rebuild a workflow tracker inside the Spec.
Rule

The world writes one TypeScript carrier for a story-altitude rule Spec stating idea, with a title, an Intent outcome, one rule and an open-question list holding one blocking question. Every value is static apart from the construct the point names: a question text or blocking flag written as a function call, or a spread of another list beside the question.

rule line 29 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:29
An open question may carry four optional fields beside its text, flag and key, namely who decides it, the links it rests on, its provisional reading and its re-entry trigger; a question without them stays lawful.
rule line 30 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:30
Who decides a question names the person, role or body whose ruling settles it. It authorizes nothing, gates no edit, and no validator compares it with the author of a change.
rule line 31 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:31
Who decides a question is one lowercase kebab token the corpus owns, on the grammar a role uses, such as owner or delegated. The graph holds no person or role to point at, so the value references nothing, and the Protocol ships no list of values.
rule line 32 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:32
In the Markdown carrier the four fields ride labelled sub-items indented under the question's own line, decider:, links:, provisional: and trigger:, each at most once and each one line, so the question line stays as authored. They are the only indented field lines the body grammar admits, and the TypeScript carrier carries the same four fields on the question object.
rule.fieldFailureError line 33 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:33
In the TypeScript carrier, a value under any of the four fields that cannot be read statically is an extraction error at that field, and the Spec's whole open-question list drops with it.

no example exercises it

rule.droppedListWarning line 34 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:34
In the TypeScript carrier, a question text or blocking flag that cannot be read statically, or a spread in the list, drops the Spec's whole open-question list, blocking questions included, with the lossy warning extract/non-static-section; only a failure under the four fields is an error.

spec:model.open-question-fields.dropped-list-warns · enabled

rule line 35 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:35
A link is a Spec id or an entry address the question rests on, and nothing else. Each is checked as a mention is: a missing target or entry is an error, and a target with no declared relation either way raises the conformance/prose-mentions warning for that pair. A link mints no relation, and a document outside the graph is named in the question's text as prose, because the graph holds no identity for it to resolve.
rule line 36 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:36
The provisional reading is one line stating what the design assumes while the question is open. It is intent, never a ruling.
rule line 37 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:37
A question carries at most one provisional line. A worked proposal for settling it is a decision Spec whose Decision section holds its decision, context, rationales, alternatives and consequences, stated at the rung its record earns. Each shaped Spec names it through decidedBy, so a decision below defined holds that Spec below ready under the typed-dependency floor.
rule line 38 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:38
A re-entry trigger is one line naming what brings a deferred Spec back, such as a named reader the shipped views do not serve. It sits on the blocking question that holds the deferral, and the open-question register reports questions that carry one apart from design holds, so no reader tells the two apart by their wording.
rule line 39 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:39
An open question carries no status, date, blocked work unit or record of who checked it. A settled question leaves the Spec, a ruling that passes the ADR three-part test lands as a decision Spec the shaped Specs name through decidedBy, and the rest of the history stays in git and in the adopter's own records.
rule line 40 · specs/model/open-question-fields.sdp.md:40
Whether a question holds the readiness floor stays its [blocking] flag alone; none of the four fields moves a floor.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.adopt-the-nouns

    The Protocol adopts established delivery nouns and rejects process state-machine and lifecycle gating.

  • spec:decisions.planning-truths-placement

    Each planning-truth type lives in its ruled home. Work-item dependency truth rides dependsOn edges, with independence as absence of the edge and scheduling phrases never authored. Decision gates live on decision-kind Specs, linked by decidedBy. Do-not-reopen rows split by what they carry: a tradeoff refusal becomes a decision-kind Spec, which a later decision that supersedes it replaces whole and a later decision that refines it narrows for one case, either under the ADR three-part test; a row that restates a behavior guarantee already homed on a carrying Spec stays on that Spec and changes by ordinary Spec revision; a hold stays a blocking open question on its own Spec and is never minted as a decision. A lawful non-decision stays in the plan record as evidence. A deferral carries its re-entry trigger in the trigger field of its own blocking open question, and declares dependsOn separately when a true precondition exists. Exclusive ownership is one Spec identity per deliverable with consumers depending on it. Selection-pressure heuristics are advisory only, carried as behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec or in recipes. Session law splits separately, across behavior rules on the graph-first planning Spec, the delivery-session on-ramp's handoff rule, and the plan file. The briefs index shape is retired as a carrier of law.

4. An authored relation may carry its reason

spec:model.relation-reasons

An authored relation may carry its reason

spec:model.relation-reasonsBusiness Rule · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 5 design entries · no pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design let a relation say why it holds: a rationale on refines, a strength on dependsOn, an aspect on constrainedBy and a reason on supersedes (docs/lineage/v0-design/01-core-primitives.md §4; 04-authoring-surfaces.md §1.3). The Protocol's relations carry a type, a target and a claim; a relation without a reason leaves the explanation of why a Spec rests on another in narrative prose a reader has to find. The prose-ownership decision gives free prose a typed owner; this Spec gives a relation's reason its home on that relation.

The first adopter meets the reverse case. When its mention audit reported Spec pairs named in prose with no relation behind them, it declared the relations that were missing dependencies and kept the rest as prose, each listed with a one-line reason no typed relation fits (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-01.md, "The mention warnings were mostly missing edges"; libar-platform/design/tools/prose-mentions.json). A reason on a relation says why an edge holds; a listed mention reason says why none does.

Intent
problem
A reviewer reading a relation cannot see why it holds, and a reviewer reading a mention left as prose cannot tell an intended pointer from a forgotten dependency without a list kept outside the graph.
outcome
Let an author say in one line why a Spec refines, depends on, is constrained by, is decided by or supersedes another, beside the relation itself.
Rule
rule line 23 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:23
An authored relation may carry one optional reason, a single line of prose owned by that relation from that Spec to that target.
rule line 24 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:24
One optional reason serves every relation type. No strength, aspect or other attribute rides a relation, except the rule keys an example's verifies lists, which the rule-coverage recipe reads.
rule line 25 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:25
A reason is intent, as its relation is; it confers no delivery fact, moves no readiness floor and changes nothing its edge confers, and a relation without one stays lawful.
rule line 26 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:26
In the envelope a relation target is a plain Spec id or an object with target and optional reason; a declared verifies object may also carry exercises. A target-only object reads as the plain id, plain ids and objects may mix in one relation, and no target is written twice. The TypeScript carrier passes the same reason beside the target.
rule line 27 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:27
A reason on supersedes says what the newer decision replaces, and a reason on a refines from one decision to another says which part of the older decision the newer one narrows.
rule line 28 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:28
A reason reaches readers with its relation through the graph, so a projection or a recipe reads it from the edge and never from the carrier.
rule line 29 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:29
A mention left as prose carries no reason in the Spec. A corpus may keep the mentions it intends as rows of from, to and reason beside its Specs and pass them to the mention audit as a parameter; the audit reports the pairs a row matches apart from the rest, each with its reason, and lists the rows that match no current pair, while the validator reads no such list and its warning stands.

7 unkeyed rules.

Design
envelopeTarget line 33 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:33
a relation target is a Spec id or { target: <spec id>, reason: <one line> }, the two mixing in one list and a single target taking either form; a declared verifies object may also carry exercises, and an object with another key, an empty reason, or a reason on two lines is refused; an object carrying only target reads as the plain id.
builderArgument line 34 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:34
each TypeScript relation builder takes an optional second argument, dependsOn(target, { reason }), with verifies(target, { reason, exercises }) also taking the rule keys, and a builder called without it writes a plain declared relation.
edgeReason line 35 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:35
an authored graph edge carries an optional reason, and the reader's relation ends carry it; the guarantees recipe (3), dependency footing (21), the planning slice (19) and the decision register (31) show it beside the relation.
gherkinRelations line 36 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:36
no Gherkin form is invented for a relation reason, because relation tags carry no prose; a Spec that needs one is authored in Markdown or TypeScript.
intendedMentions line 37 · specs/model/relation-reasons.sdp.md:37
the mention audit (recipe 22) takes params.intended, rows { from, to, reason } keyed by Spec ids, and returns intended, the unbacked pairs a row matches with its reason, kept apart from the remaining pairs, and staleIntended, the rows that match no current pair.

5. Designs are compared between a base commit and the working tree at entry grain

spec:consumers.design-diff

Designs are compared between a base commit and the working tree at entry grain

spec:consumers.design-diffUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 8 design entries · 4 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design compared graph snapshots. Comparison concerns the curated graph a design lives in and needs no symbol identity.

Iterating on a design asks what changed since the last reading. The first adopter asks for a comparison by Spec id, section and entry key that tells changed declaration text from changed prose, moved entries, readiness edits, relation edits and new or removed examples, and for what changed since a design pass, read against the commit that pass read (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-02.md, items 30 and 31). Git shows the changed lines; this comparison shows the changed design.

Intent
actor
A reviewer or an agent starting the next design pass over a Pack, holding the commit the last pass read.
problem
A line diff of the carriers shows edits but not which Specs, entries, questions and relations changed, so each pass re-reads the whole Pack to find what moved.
outcome
Show what changed in a design between a base commit and the working tree, down to the Spec, section and keyed entry, so a reviewer reads what changed since the last pass.
Behavior
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:28
The design diff compares a base graph with the current graph.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:29
A comparison is a catalog recipe that takes the graph sdp build wrote at the base commit as a recipe parameter and compares it with the graph the evaluation derives from the working tree, including uncommitted edits; it adds no verb or binding.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:30
The base graph is input the caller holds, derived from the repository alone at the base commit; it never answers in the graph's name, and the comparison writes nothing.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:31
The caller always names the base. The recipe reads no record of a design pass and keeps none, and a corpus that notes which commit a pass read keeps that note outside the graph.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:32
Two graphs written by different engine versions are compared on what both carry; the result reports each side's schema version, and a difference is a diagnostic in the result, never a refusal.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:33
It reports the Specs added and removed, and for a Spec present in both graphs the changes to its title, kind, altitude, stated readiness, relations, narrative and each section.
rule line 34 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:34
Inside the Design and UI sections, the open questions and other keyed sections apart from rules and flows, it compares keyed entries by key and reports each as added, removed, changed in value or moved in order.
rule line 35 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:35
Rule and flow entries match first by unchanged text, preferring the same key for repeated wording, then by retained key; remaining unkeyed base entries pair in list order, including an entry reworded while adding a key. An unmatched keyed base entry is removed, and an unmatched head entry is added. Other unkeyed entries have no identity across the two graphs and compare as part of their whole section.
rule line 36 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:36
A rule or flow with unchanged text whose key was added, removed or changed is one keyed change naming its old and new address, or none; only a text change is changed. An unchanged entry moving between rules and flows is moved; when one graph keeps no order across rules and flows, keyed entries compare by order within each list and a ruleOrder diagnostic names the Spec.
rule line 37 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:37
It reports changes to Pack membership, member order and what a Pack's order means, and to the code units, verifiers and delivery facts bound to each Spec, kept apart from the authored changes because they derive from anchors.
rule line 38 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:38
A comparison states facts about the two graphs and confers nothing. It grants no approval, raises no staleness flag, moves no readiness and never records that a pass happened.

11 unkeyed rules.

diffRecipe line 42 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:42
recipe 35, the design diff, takes params.base, the graph object sdp build wrote at the base commit, an optional params.pack that limits the comparison to the Specs that are members of that Pack at either commit, and params.detail; it compares params.base with the graph binding and reads nothing else.
diffShape line 43 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:43
{ base: { schemaVersion, specs }, head: { schemaVersion, specs }, diagnostics, totals, specs: { added: [id], removed: [id], changed }, packs, bindings, leftOut }, where totals counts each list and diagnostics lists schema-version differences, parts outside the common schema, a Pack absent from both graphs, and Specs compared without order across rules and flows; base.specs and head.specs count the Specs of the comparison scope present on each side, the scope being every Spec or, with pack, the Pack's members in either graph, while the top-level specs object carries the change lists.

changedSpecRow line 44 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:44
{ id, parts: [part] } in the summary and { id, parts: [{ part, change, from, to }] } with detail: true; change is added, removed, changed, moved or keyed. For keyed, from and to carry the old and new entry addresses, null meaning none; other changes carry the values on each side, a rule or flow value as { list, text }. A text change while adding a key is one changed entry.

no citation recorded

diffParts line 45 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:45
a part is title, specKind, altitude, statedReadiness, narrative, relation.<type>:<target>, a keyed entry as design.<key>, ui.<key>, question.<key>, rule.<key> or term.<term>, an unkeyed rule or flow as behavior.rules[<index>] or behavior.flows[<index>], using its head index; a removed unkeyed entry uses its base index with a (base) mark, such as behavior.rules[1] (base), so it cannot share a name with a head entry at that index; an unkeyed question list as intent.openQuestions, and any other section as its name.
movedEntry line 46 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:46
a keyed entry whose value is unchanged and whose position among the keyed entries of its section changed is moved; an entry whose value changed is changed whatever its position. For rules and flows, unchanged text with a different key takes keyed precedence, then a list change or relative order change among retained entries is moved; anonymous entries compare order within their list. Adding or removing a key alone moves no other entry.
packRows line 47 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:47
packs rows are { id, change, membersAdded, membersRemoved, reordered, orderChanged, orderBefore, orderAfter } for each Pack added, removed or changed in membership, member order or order meaning; orderBefore and orderAfter are "reading" or "priority", null on a side where the Pack is absent, and orderChanged is true when both sides hold the Pack and the two differ. An absent order reads as "reading" in every schema version; a value the head's engine does not know is outside the common schema, listed in diagnostics and not compared; that Pack's membership and member order still compare, its orderChanged is false, and the side holding the unknown value reads null.

bindingRows line 48 · specs/consumers/design-diff.sdp.md:48
bindings rows are { id, implementedBy, referencedBy, verifiers, deliveryFacts }, each an { added, removed } pair of ids or fact names, kept apart from specs because they derive from anchors.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.roadmap-priority

    A roadmap is a Pack whose manifest states order: priority; its members' authored order is the corpus's advisory priority, first entry first. order is an optional manifest field whose one lawful value is priority, and a Pack without it keeps the reading order every Pack has. Priority is preference among bodies of work and nothing more: it carries no date, no dependency, no status and no gate, and no check, recipe or page treats a place on a roadmap as permission, obligation or sequence. Everything a roadmap shows about an entry, what it still needs and what holds it, is read from the graph each time. A corpus may keep several roadmaps, and a Spec may be listed on any number of them.

6. A context bundle is composed per invocation within a stated budget

spec:consumers.context-bundle

A context bundle is composed per invocation within a stated budget

spec:consumers.context-bundleUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:adopter-speed-v1, pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 17 design entries · 7 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle present.

The original design precomputed graph slices for different reading scopes and a prompt bundle for one Spec. The Protocol keeps context bundle for the reading material of one design pass, composed on demand.

The first adopter's design passes assemble the same reading material by hand: the Pack design, member questions, dependency footing, pinned declarations and carrying Spec text where the graph answer falls short. Its perspectives read the same Pack for different concerns. The agent front door composes a bundle on each invocation; the bundle is never a committed answer in the graph's name. It builds on Pack design.

At an adopter's scale a bundle is mostly structure, so its shape is compact. Each member and each example row names its carrier file once. A cut entry without an entry address keeps only its line, since its row and its place in the bundle already name it. A question, a pinned value or a member example's steps appears in one place. Pinned declarations stay whole by default, because a builder and a test author hold to them. A caller whose scope still does not fit may let the bundle cut them to their entry addresses, and then reads each one in its Spec when the pass needs it. A partial bundle stays refused, because a bundle missing members would read as the whole scope.

A scope can hold more design than one budget allows after every cut, as the first adopter's largest Packs do. A caller then reads the bundle in parts: the same bundle, split between members into ordered parts that each fit the budget, whose members together are the whole scope. In parts a cut is taken only when an item, a member or the boundary, does not fit a part by itself, so a part keeps the design a single bundle would have cut. A repeated header that exceeds the budget alone is named as one oversized item; otherwise each item that exceeds the budget alone is named. No part is returned in either case.

Intent
actor
An agent starting one design pass over a Pack or an ordered list of Specs.
problem
Each pass assembles the same reading material by running the same recipes and joining their answers by hand, and nothing bounds what it hands the model.
outcome
Give an agent the reading material for one design pass in one composed slice of the graph within a stated budget, so no session hand-assembles it.
Behavior
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:27
A bundle is a catalog recipe that takes its scope and its budget as recipe parameters; it adds no entrance and no query verb.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:28
A bundle is composed from the graph on each invocation by the reader every recipe uses; nothing is precomputed, saved or committed, and two invocations over the same graph with the same parameters compose the same bundle.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:29
A bundle takes one scope: pack, a Pack id, or specs, an ordered list of Spec ids. For specs the members are the listed Specs in the given order and the boundary is each member's one-hop neighbors through the four typed relations both ways, with verifies and supersedes apart, as the Pack boundary is built. Both scopes or neither is a diagnostic result. A changeset fills specs from the impacted Spec ids changed-file impact reports, and a Pack's open questions are read from the Pack bundle, not from a third scope.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:30
With pack, a bundle may take members, an ordered subset of the Pack's member ids, which the perspective filter returns; it keeps the Pack's framing and boundary, lists only those members in that order, and states that it is a subset, so one filter implementation serves both recipes.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:31
A bundle for a Pack carries the Pack design assembly, its members in authored order with their design columns and its boundary, then each member's open questions with their addresses and lines, its dependency footing, its pinned declarations and its examples.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:32
The budget is a hard limit on a successful bundle, counted in UTF-16 code units, the length a recipe body reads, of the compact JSON.stringify of the value the recipe returns, its scope, budget and left-out statement included; sdp q --json prints a longer indented form, and the budget never measures printed text. The bundle also reports a token estimate labeled as an estimate, so no model's tokenizer binds the Protocol.
rule.oneCopy line 33 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:33
A bundle carries a member's open questions only in its questions, a pinned declaration's value only in its member's Design section, and an example's steps only in its own member row when the example is a member of the bundle; an example outside the bundle keeps its steps in the row of each member it refines or verifies.

no example exercises it

rule.cutOrder line 34 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:34
When the scope exceeds the budget, the bundle cuts in a fixed order and stops at the first cut after which it fits: boundary rows down to their ids, footing rows down to their ids, member narrative, example step text, non-blocking question text, remaining section values other than pinned declarations, then, only when the caller allows it, pinned declarations down to their entry addresses. It never cuts member ids, the stated rung, the floor reached, the stated next rung, blocking questions or entry addresses, and it cuts nothing else.

no example exercises it

rule.declarationAddresses line 35 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:35
A caller allows the last cut by passing declarations: "addresses"; without it, or with declarations: "whole", pinned declarations stay whole, and any other value is a diagnostic result.

rule line 36 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:36
Without part, when the protected content alone exceeds the budget after every permitted cut, the recipe returns a budget-exceeded result as data and no partial bundle: the requested scope, the budget, and the minimum count the protected content needs in the same unit; sdp q exits 0, because the result is the body's return and not a refusal.
rule line 37 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:37
A bundle gives the file and line of an entry or a binding in place of a source excerpt, because the reader never reads source.
rule line 38 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:38
A bundle states its scope, its budget and what it left out to stay within the budget, so a reader knows what to read in the Specs themselves.
rule line 39 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:39
A bundle carries facts from the graph and no instructions of its own; the brief that tells an agent what to look for stays the corpus's own text.
rule.parts line 40 · specs/consumers/context-bundle.sdp.md:40
With part, the 1-based index of the part to return, a bundle comes in ordered parts, each within the budget, and the members of its parts, read in part order, are the bundle's members in order, each once.

7. A Pack is read from a named perspective

spec:consumers.review-perspectives

A Pack is read from a named perspective

spec:consumers.review-perspectivesUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 4 design entries · 1 pinned declaration · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design gave every reader one reading surface, each reading from their own concern: the analyst, the domain engineer, the architect, the tester, the designer and the agent (docs/lineage/v0-design/04-authoring-surfaces.md §6). The first adopter iterates each capability's design through advisor lenses, its runtime platform, the domain, operations and the product, each a written list of the questions its field asks, run over the same Pack by the same pass brief (libar-platform/design/advisors/lenses/, libar-platform/design/advisors/task-pass.md). It asks for a lens to be a filter over the same capability that reorders and emphasizes questions, entries, examples and constraints and opens the same Specs, with no new Spec kind and no compulsory sequence of stages (libar-platform/docs/feedback/sdp-feedback-02.md, item 28). The Protocol takes the member filter and the order and leaves each member's content whole; emphasis inside a member stays the reader's.

The owner ruled the word: perspective. The Spec Studio keeps lens for its graph views, its Packs, capabilities, architecture, tests and evidence views, and discipline stays the filter by kind or section. The adopter's advisor lens is a reader's concern, not a view of the graph, so in the Protocol's terms it is a perspective.

Intent
actor
A reviewer or an agent who reads a Pack for one concern, such as the domain model, operations or the runtime platform.
problem
Every reading of a Pack shows every member in the same order with the same emphasis, so a reader with one concern sorts it by hand, and an adopter keeps its perspectives as prose briefs the graph cannot apply.
outcome
Let a reviewer read the same Pack from one perspective at a time, filtered and ordered for that perspective, without a new kind or a stage.
Behavior
rule.contentIntact line 22 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:22
A perspective filters and orders a Pack's members and leaves each selected member's content intact; every row opens the same Spec, and the whole Pack stays one step away.

no example exercises it

rule line 23 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:23
A perspective adds no kind, readiness, stage or sequence; reading a Pack from one perspective records nothing, and no perspective is required before another or before ready is stated.
rule line 24 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:24
The corpus owns its perspectives and their questions; the Protocol supplies the filter and ships no list of perspectives.
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:25
A perspective is corpus data: a JSON object the corpus keeps beside its briefs and passes to the perspective filter, a catalog recipe, through --params. The reader loads no perspective file, and no validator lists or checks perspectives, so no registry forms.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:26
A perspective selects members by Spec id or id prefix, kind, section presence, Design key with an optional value, question key, and authored relation type with a stated direction; it selects component layer or context only through the member's code unit bindings, satisfying or referencing, that the perspective names; it infers nothing from prose, paths or imports.
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:27
A member selected by a Design key, including the layer and context keys a component design states, is selected on declared intent; a member selected through a binding's component is selected on anchored structure; each row names which, and the two are never merged into one architecture answer.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:28
Values within one selector are alternatives and different selectors combine as requirements; an unsupported selector is a diagnostic in the result, and a valid selector that matches nothing is an explicit empty result.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:29
Members keep the manifest's authored order unless the perspective gives an explicit priority order, authored order breaking ties; every selected member's blocking questions stay visible whatever else the perspective filters out.

7 unkeyed rules.

Design
perspectiveObject line 33 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:33
{ "name": "models", "select": { "kinds": ["model"] } } selects the members of kind model. A perspective is { name, select, order } with select and order optional, and its selectors are ids, idPrefixes, kinds, sections, designKeys, questionKeys, relations and bindings, each optional; different selectors combine as requirements. An absent selector imposes no requirement, a present empty list matches no member, and an absent or empty select object selects every member. A designKeys item is { key, value } with value optional; a relations item is { type, direction, target } with direction out or in and target optional; bindings is { via, layers, contexts }, where via is required and lists satisfies or references, and absent layers or contexts impose no restriction. order lists Spec ids by priority, authored order breaking ties.

no citation recorded

perspectiveRecipe line 34 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:34
recipe 37, the perspective filter, takes params.pack and params.perspective and returns { pack, perspective, totals: { members, selected }, diagnostics, selected, notSelected }.
perspectiveRows line 35 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:35
each selected row is { id, matchedOn: [{ selector, value, claim }], blockingQuestions: [{ address, question }] } in the perspective's order and then authored order; claim is declared for a match on authored intent and anchored for a match through a binding; notSelected lists the remaining member ids in authored order.
perspectiveDiagnostics line 36 · specs/consumers/review-perspectives.sdp.md:36
an unknown selector, a value of the wrong type or a bindings selector with no via is a diagnostic row { selector, problem }, and the recipe still applies the selectors it understood.

8. A change proposal is addressed, based and checked before it lands

spec:consumers.intent-composition.proposal

A change proposal is addressed, based and checked before it lands

spec:consumers.intent-composition.proposalContract · storyready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:design-management-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 2 pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

The original design's patch loop made every change from a view reviewable and checked before it touched source. A patch named its target, the graph hash it was made against, a rationale, its operations and who proposed it; a CLI checked its schema and its base, applied it to a copy of the graph, ran the validators and only then rewrote the Spec files (docs/lineage/v0-design/02-system-architecture.md §2; 07-spec-studio-and-projections.md §6). The Protocol refused the patch and the codemod. A view composes scoped intent, an agent edits source as a person would, git records the edit and the same checks evaluate it. That edit model drops two things the patch loop gave: a proposed change a person can review before an agent applies it, and a guard against a proposal made against an older design.

The first adopter's agents already write proposals in that shape. A design pass returns findings that each name an entry address or a Spec section, state the gap, and propose exact text for a Spec with the entry it replaces or follows (libar-platform/design/advisors/task-pass.md), and its register tool applies a JSON patch only after checking all of it (libar-platform/design/advisors/register.md). This Spec states the reviewable half of the patch loop without the codemod. A proposal is a request that an agent applies as an ordinary edit, checked by sdp validate on a worktree before it merges. It also gives the Spec Studio's composing panel a shape to hand off.

Intent
problem
A proposed design change travels as free prose, so a reviewer cannot tell what it touches, which version of the design it read, or whether it still applies once the design has moved.
outcome
Give a proposed design change a reviewable shape: what it touches by Spec id or entry address, the commit it was read at, the change requested and why, checked on a worktree before merge.
Contract
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:25
A proposal is one JSON document on one schema, which a recipe takes as a parameter; a Markdown memo is a rendering of that document and never a second source of it.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:26
A proposal names its scope as one or more Spec ids or entry addresses, each resolved before anything is applied: a Spec id through the reader's Spec context, an entry address through address resolution.
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:27
A proposal names the commit whose graph it was read against.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:28
A proposal states the requested change in words an agent can apply, such as the exact text for an entry with the address it replaces or follows, a new open question with its flag, or a relation to declare or remove.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:29
A proposal states its reason in one line.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:30
The proposal check compares each change's scope between the proposal's base commit and the working tree through the design diff, entry by entry, and reports each change on its own row, so one changed scope never hides the state of another change; the check applies nothing and routes nothing.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:31
Applying a proposal is an ordinary source edit by an agent or a person; no tool rewrites a carrier from it, and nothing is applied to a copy of the graph first.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:32
A proposal carries no status, approval or verdict, and the graph records none; whether it was accepted is git history and the adopter's own record.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:33
A proposal carries no proposer. Whoever hands it over is its author until it is applied, and then git authorship and co-author trailers are the record; the schema refuses the field.

proposalDocument line 37 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:37
{ "schema": "sdp-proposal/1", "base": "<commit>", "reason": "<one line>", "changes": [change] }, with schema, base, reason and a non-empty changes required and no other field.

no citation recorded

proposalChange line 38 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:38
{ "scope": ["<spec id or entry address>"], "request": "<words an agent can apply>", "text": "<exact entry text>", "replaces": "<entry address>", "follows": "<entry address>", "relation": { "action": "declare", "from": "<spec id>", "type": "dependsOn", "target": "<spec id>" }, "reason": "<one line>" }, with scope non-empty and request required, replaces and follows exclusive, action either declare or remove, from naming the relation's source Spec, and no other field.

no citation recorded

proposalSchemaFile line 39 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:39
the package ships the document's JSON Schema as schemas/sdp-proposal-1.schema.json, so an agent can use it as a structured-output schema; the check recipe validates the same shape itself, and a test holds the two to the same accepted and refused samples.
checkRecipe line 40 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:40
recipe 38, the proposal check, takes params.proposal and params.base, the base graph, and returns { schemaProblems: [{ path, problem }], base, diagnostics, totals: { changes, moved, unresolved }, changes }, with the design diff's diagnostics for the Specs it compares; when the document breaks the schema or the base graph is missing it returns the problems and no change rows.
checkedScope line 41 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:41
the check resolves and compares the deduplicated union of scope, replaces, follows and relation.from, and a change row's scope reports that union, so an entry a change replaces or follows cannot move unseen.
checkRows line 42 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:42
each change row is { index, scope: [{ ref, resolvesAtHead, resolvesAtBase, moved }], moved, relationTarget }; an item's moved is true when its Spec is added or removed between the two graphs, and otherwise, for an entry address, when the entry's value is added, removed or changed, an order-only move leaving it false, or, for a whole Spec, when any of its parts changed or moved in order; the row's moved is true when any item's is; relationTarget is { ref, resolvesAtHead } for a declared relation and null otherwise.
incomparableScope line 43 · specs/consumers/intent-composition.proposal.sdp.md:43
an item outside the common schema, or an otherwise unmoved whole-Spec item whose order across rules and flows one graph does not keep, carries comparable: false and a reason in place of moved; its row carries comparable: false and a null moved unless another item moved.

9. Enrichment keeps one Spec while its detail changes

spec:model.enrichment-lifecycle

Enrichment keeps one Spec while its detail changes

spec:model.enrichment-lifecycleDomain Model · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 2 design entries · no pinned declarations · no decisions

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Intent
outcome
Keep a Spec useful after implementation without copying its detail into a second artifact that drifts from it.
Model
enrichment lifecycle line 18 · specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md:18
The same Spec gains and may later slim typed detail without changing identity or moving truth into another artifact type.
distillation boundary line 19 · specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md:19
A Design entry may leave its Spec once the Spec is implemented with a verifier and a bound artifact carries the entry: a pinned declaration whose realizing unit exists, or a bound example. Prose that explains why always stays, so each explanation keeps one home, and implemented code alone justifies neither keeping nor deleting detail.
slimming candidate line 20 · specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md:20
A Design entry past the distillation boundary. A recipe reports the candidates and never deletes one; removing an entry stays the author's edit.
Design
slimmingRecipe line 24 · specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md:24
recipe 39, slimming candidates, takes an optional params.pack and returns { totals: { specs, potentialCandidates }, rows, leftOut }, each row { spec, key, line, declaration, implementations, verifiers } for a pinned declaration on a Spec that carries both implemented and has-verifier.
slimmingScope line 25 · specs/model/enrichment-lifecycle.sdp.md:25
rows are potential candidates the author compares with the bound artifacts, because a binding names a whole Spec and the graph proves no entry-level realization for a declaration or an example; leftOut states both limits, and prose entries are never candidates.

10. File-level imports show where curation is missing

spec:consumers.impact-graph.curation-assist

File-level imports show where curation is missing

spec:consumers.impact-graph.curation-assistUse Case / Behavior · featureready floor ready

Packs: pack:design-iteration-v1, pack:self-hosting-v1

Design: 7 design entries · 4 pinned declarations · 1 decision

Findings: no errors, no warnings

specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md

No open questions and no blocking questions; implementation binding present, verifier binding present, and expected-outcome oracle none.

Gen 1 of this tool, @libar-dev/architect, derived a mechanical import graph beside its curated one and used it to show authors where curation was missing: load-bearing modules no anchor covered, coverage by package, and designed modules no code realized yet. The idea held; the build did not. It hard-coded the repository's layout into the engine, read TypeScript only, and mixed both graphs in one query handle. A review of gen 1 found that the file-level layer gave most of its curation value and that only symbol queries need a symbol identity, which the impact graph's symbol-reach child holds open, so the file-level layer stands on its own.

Intent
actor
An author curating anchors across a codebase, or a design pass over a large redesign.
problem
Nothing tells an author which load-bearing files no anchor covers, where anchored uses and the code's imports disagree, or which component designs no code realizes yet, so curation gaps surface only when someone reads the code.
outcome
Report from file-level imports where anchors and component designs are missing or drifting, as advice that never authors intent.
Behavior
rule line 25 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:25
The layer reads file-level import edges from a per-language adapter and identifies each file by its repository-relative path, so it needs no symbol identity.
rule line 26 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:26
Every import relationship it derives is inferred; the imports file's schema and the recipe's external-inferred-input label carry that claim for all of them at once, so no relationship carries its own. The relationships stay apart from the curated graph: no uses, memberOf, satisfies or delivery fact derives from them, and a query of the curated graph never reads them unless the caller asks.
rule line 27 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:27
It reports the files with the highest import fan-in that no anchor covers, the anchored uses edges between two components whose files share no import, the imports between two anchored components that no uses states, and the component designs no component: anchor realizes yet.
rule line 28 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:28
Every report is advice: it refuses nothing, fails no validation and authors no anchor, and an author who agrees edits an anchor or a Spec as usual.
rule line 29 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:29
The engine reads no repository layout convention: source roots and module resolution come from the adapter's configuration, and a file belongs to a component only when it holds that component: anchor or a code anchor memberOf it, never through a path pattern in the engine.
rule line 30 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:30
The TypeScript adapter reads imports through the compiler library extraction already depends on; another language arrives as another adapter.
rule line 31 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:31
The adapter runs outside extraction and outside sdp q: sdp build, given the adapter's configuration, writes the import edges to generated/imports.json, sorted and without a timestamp, and the curation recipe reads that file through --params, so no query derives imports and no validator sees an inferred edge.
rule line 32 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:32
The imports configuration accepts optional root-relative exclude paths matching a file or directory subtree, refuses unknown keys, and records exclusions in its output so curation distinguishes deliberate omissions from missing input.
rule line 33 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:33
The recipe labels the file as external inferred input and reports a file present on one side only; it states nothing in the graph's name.
rule line 34 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:34
The adapter follows re-exports through barrel files, so a uses that reaches a component through an index file counts as backed by an import.
rule line 35 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:35
Load-bearing is a ranked list, not a threshold: the recipe reports each uncovered file's import fan-in and fan-out, takes a limit, and leaves the cut to the caller.

11 unkeyed rules.

Design
importsFlag line 39 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:39
sdp build --imports PATH names the adapter configuration, a JSON object { "adapter": "typescript", "tsconfig": "tsconfig.json", "roots": ["src"], "exclude": ["src/generated"] } with root-relative paths, where exclude is optional and each of its paths names a file or a directory subtree, and a key outside these four is refused; without the flag the build writes no imports file and leaves an existing one untouched.

no citation recorded

importsFile line 40 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:40
{ "schema": "sdp-imports/1", "adapter": "typescript", "exclude": ["src/generated"], "files": [{ "file": "src/a.ts", "imports": ["src/b.ts"] }] } in generated/imports.json, files and imports sorted in code-unit order, paths root-relative with POSIX separators, exclude recording the configuration's exclusions in that form and sorted, every file the adapter reads under the configured roots and outside the exclusions listed even when it imports nothing, and imports outside the roots or under an exclusion left out. The schema and the recipe's external inferred input label give every listed relationship the inferred claim.

no citation recorded

barrelImports line 41 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:41
when a file imports a barrel that re-exports another file, its imports lists the barrel and every file the barrel's re-exports reach, so the list is already the backing a uses check reads; a barrel under an exclusion is left out of the list while the files reached through it stay.
importForms line 42 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:42
the TypeScript adapter reads the .ts, .cts, .mts and .tsx files under the configured roots and the module references the compiler resolves in them: import and export-from declarations, type-only and side-effect imports included, import x = require(...), and import(...) calls and import types with a literal specifier; a computed specifier and a plain require(...) call are not read.
curationRecipe line 43 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:43
recipe 40, the curation report, takes params.imports, the imports file's object, and params.limit, 20 by default, and returns { input, totals, uncovered, usesWithoutImport, importsWithoutUses, unrealizedComponents, oneSided }.
curationRows line 44 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:44
uncovered rows are { file, fanIn, fanOut } for files no anchor sits in, ranked by fan-in then path and cut at limit; usesWithoutImport rows are { from, to, fromComponent, toComponent }; importsWithoutUses rows are { fromComponent, toComponent, imports, sample: { from, to } }; unrealizedComponents rows are { spec, componentId } for component designs with no resolving anchored satisfies edge from the planned component: unit to the design, so an existing id without that binding stays unrealized.

no citation recorded

curationInput line 45 · specs/consumers/impact-graph.curation-assist.sdp.md:45
input is { label: "external inferred input", schema, adapter, exclude, files }, with exclude echoing the imports file's exclusions, and oneSided lists anchored source files the imports file does not list and imports-file entries outside every anchored component, so a stale or partial file shows.

Decisions

  • spec:decisions.architectural-annotation

    Architectural significance is annotated on the anchor of the unit that realizes it. A code anchor may carry role, the architectural pattern the unit plays; a component: anchor may additionally carry layer, one of edge, application, domain, adapter, or infrastructure, and context, its bounded context. The component: anchor is anchored architecture: it is the declared component, and there is no separate architecture file, because the anchor sits where the component is realized. It is not the original design's declared Component that could exist before code; an unrealized component lives in Specs and never as an invented CodeNode. A role is a free, corpus-owned vocabulary whose taxonomy the census renders with counts from the graph; service, decider, projection, read-model, codec, contract, barrel, and utility are the lineage set, not a closed list. layer is a closed set, and a value outside it is an envelope error; layer or context on a non-component anchor is an envelope error. All three attributes are optional, and omission is lawful.
